land.text: the Basque provinces (Gipuzkoa, Alava, Biscay) and Navarre, where 'the Carlists managed to erect a temporary state'

predecessors.note: Carlist control began with the uprising of 21 April 1872 under the monarchy; the temporary state with its capital at Estella dates from August 1873.

land.text: the Basque provinces and Navarre, retaken by the army in February 1876

successors.note: 'On February 19, government forces drove through the weak Carlist forces protecting Estella, taking the city'; Carlos VII left Spain on 28 February 1876.

capitals.name: Estella
capitals.note: 'in August, Carlist forces captured the city of Estella', which became their capital and seat of a provisional government under Carlos VII; taken by government forces on 19 February 1876. In Catalonia the Carlists 'set their capital at Olot' (March 1874).

rulers.name: Carlos VII
rulers.title: Carlist pretender
rulers.note: Led the provisional government at Estella; retreated to France after Orokieta in May 1872 and left Spain for good on 28 February 1876.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1873-1875: the Carlists 'managed to erect a temporary state' in the Basque region (Gipuzkoa, Alava, Biscay and Navarre) with Estella as capital; on 24 September 1874 'Carlists still held the Basque Provinces and most of Navarre'. They failed to take Bilbao (siege 21 February - 2 May 1874) and San Sebastian. The page gives no area, so no infobox check; the region is the whole of the four provinces, which overstates the held part where Bilbao and San Sebastian stayed loyal.

correction.text: the Basque provinces and Navarre as held by the Carlist state; the cities of Bilbao and San Sebastian never fell

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1876: after Estella fell on 19 February 1876 nothing was left; the state is drawn only to the end of February 1876 (shrunk to the Navarrese north). Catalonia, Aragon, the Maestrazgo and Valencia ('the Carlist cause ... had been successful since the initial uprising in 1872') are guerrilla ground, a contested zone in the Spanish dossiers, not state territory; the Maestrazgo 'small state' at Cantavieja was undated and fell 'later'.

correction.text: Navarre, the last Carlist ground in February 1876

ledger.note: 1873: Catalonia is fought over. the rebels 'controlled most of the Basque Country, Navarre, and Catalonia without opposition' (the page's sentence carries no year; it sits in the 1873 narrative after the cantonal rising; quote corrected by reviewer eu-20-n); in March 1874 the Carlists captured Olot and 'set their capital at Olot' with a government at San Joan de les Abadesses.

August 1873: the Carlists take Estella and set up a provisional government. 'in August, Carlist forces captured the city of Estella', which became their capital and seat of a provisional government under Carlos VII; 'the Carlists managed to erect a temporary state' in Gipuzkoa, Alava, Biscay and Navarre. The rebellion itself began on 21 April 1872; the page gives the state no founding day, so August 1873 (Estella) stands for it.

region.text: the Basque provinces and Navarre, held by the Carlist army

ledger.note: December 1874: the Republic ends with the Restoration ('in December 1874, a military coup installed a new Bourbon monarch', Alfonso XII); the contest over Catalonia goes on with the monarchy.

December 1874: the war goes on against the restored monarchy. Alfonso XII is proclaimed on 29 December 1874 (First Spanish Republic page); 'Carlists still held the Basque Provinces and most of Navarre' on 24 September 1874.

19 February 1876: Estella falls. 'On February 19, government forces drove through the weak Carlist forces protecting Estella, taking the city'; the loss of the capital 'convinced the Carlists their cause was lost'.
28 February 1876: the war ends. 'Carlos VII left Spain on February 28', the same day Alfonso XII entered Pamplona; he went into exile in France.
28 February 1876: the Carlist state ends. Carlos VII leaves Spain; infobox of the war: '21 April 1872 - 28 February 1876'.

wars.name: Third Carlist War

zones.text: the Basque provinces, Navarre and Catalonia

wars.outcome: Government victory: Estella fell on 19 February 1876 and Carlos VII left Spain on 28 February 1876; the Carlists besieged Bilbao from 21 February to 2 May 1874 and failed.

certainty.note: A rebel state with moving front lines; the held ground shifted with every campaign and the cities never fell.

sources.title: Third Carlist War
sources.note: Carlist temporary state, Estella (August 1873, 19 February 1876), Olot (March 1874), Maestrazgo, Bilbao siege, end 28 February 1876.

sources.title: First Spanish Republic
sources.note: Carlist control of the Basque Country, Navarre and Catalonia in 1873; Restoration 29 December 1874.

notes: A rebel state written because the First Spanish Republic dossier (first-spanish-republic) names it as counterpart (loss 1873-08, contest 1873-1874); no Cliopatria row covers it. Wikipedia has no 'Carlist State' article that was opened; wikipedia and wikidata are null. The extent is the four provinces, which overstates what was held; the page gives no frontier or area. Page silent: the exact founding day of the provisional government; the Maestrazgo state's dates (undated, 'a small state in the Maestrat ... later capitulated after a siege'); San Joan de les Abadesses and Olot dates beyond March 1874. The first Carlist war and Second Carlist War are outside this dossier. The kingdom-of-spain dossier carries no Carlist events: its 1873 loss and 1874 gain are for the Republic. Gazetteer: all names resolve.
